# Learn, share and grow with [R]{.accent} in Tanzania {.hero-title .unnumbered .unlisted}

::: {.lead}
A community for everyone in Tanzania who uses R or wants to learn it: students, researchers, analysts, statisticians and developers. We meet in person and online to share skills, solve problems together and put data to work for our communities.
:::

::: {.hero-actions}
[Join the community](join.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg}
[See upcoming events](events.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-tz .btn-lg}
:::
:::

``` r
library(tidyverse)

# Everyone is welcome, whatever your level
tz_r_users |>
  filter(curious) |>
  mutate(skills = learn_together(skills)) |>
  summarise(impact = sum(shared_knowledge))
```

## Practical R skills, built together {.unnumbered}
:::
:::

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .g-col-lg-3}
::: {.feature-card}
[<i class="bi bi-people-fill"></i>]{.feature-icon .green aria-hidden="true"}

### Meetups and talks {.unnumbered}

Regular gatherings, in person and online, where members show how they use R at work, in research and in their studies.
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .g-col-lg-3}
::: {.feature-card}
[<i class="bi bi-laptop"></i>]{.feature-icon .blue aria-hidden="true"}

### Hands-on workshops {.unnumbered}

Beginner-friendly training in data cleaning, visualisation, statistics, Shiny apps, Quarto reports and more.
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .g-col-lg-3}
::: {.feature-card}
[<i class="bi bi-chat-heart"></i>]{.feature-icon .yellow aria-hidden="true"}

### Learning together {.unnumbered}

Study groups, a shared resource library and a friendly place to ask questions, from your first `install.packages()` onwards.
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .g-col-lg-3}
::: {.feature-card}
[<i class="bi bi-globe-europe-africa"></i>]{.feature-icon .dark aria-hidden="true"}

### Data for Tanzania {.unnumbered}

Using R with local data on health, agriculture, education, the economy and the environment, and sharing what we learn.
:::
:::

## You're welcome here, whatever your level {.unnumbered}

Whether you write R every day or have never opened RStudio, there's a place for you. Conversations happen in English and Kiswahili.
:::
:::

::: {.audience-list}
- Students
- Researchers and academics
- Public health and epidemiology
- Agriculture and environment
- Government and NGO analysts
- Statisticians
- Data scientists and developers
- Complete beginners
:::
